theory.title: Pronombres recíprocos each other y one another
theory.explanation: Usa each other y one another cuando dos o más personas realizan una acción mutuamente. Expresan una relación recíproca: We help each other (nos ayudamos mutuamente); the teams respect one another (los equipos se respetan entre sí).
theory.tip: Each other / one another = mutuamente, entre sí.

content.passage: The exchange programme brought together students from four countries. At first, they were shy, but they soon began helping each other with language practice. They shared meals, taught one another new expressions and learned about different traditions. The teachers encouraged them to listen to one another and ask questions. By the end of the programme, the students had become good friends and promised to stay in touch.

items.prompt: Describe how friends help each other.
items.modelAnswer: Friends help each other by listening, sharing practical advice and offering support during difficult times. When I moved house, my friends carried boxes and helped me unpack. Their help made a stressful day much easier.

items.prompt: Talk about how people can learn from one another.
items.modelAnswer: People can learn from one another by sharing experiences and explaining different ways of doing things. At work, a new colleague taught me a useful computer shortcut, and I showed him how to organise customer records.

items.prompt: Explain how two communities might support each other.
items.modelAnswer: Two neighbouring communities might support each other by sharing sports facilities and organising joint cultural events. They could also create a group to help older residents or collect food for families in need.

items.prompt: Describe a time people shared ideas with each other.
items.modelAnswer: During a planning meeting, we shared ideas about how to improve the local park. One person suggested more benches, while another recommended a children's play area. We combined the ideas and created a better plan.

items.prompt: How can students teach one another?
items.modelAnswer: Students can teach one another by working in pairs and explaining topics in their own words. A student who understands a grammar point can give an example, while their partner can help with pronunciation.

items.prompt: Talk about how neighbours look after one another.
items.modelAnswer: Neighbours look after one another by collecting parcels, watering plants and checking on people who live alone. These small actions create trust and make the street feel safer.

items.prompt: Explain why people should listen to each other.
items.modelAnswer: People should listen to each other because everyone has different experiences and information. If we listen carefully, we may discover a solution that we hadn't considered. It also shows respect.

items.prompt: Describe a group that respects one another.
items.modelAnswer: Our book club is a group where members respect one another even when they choose different books. Everyone gets time to explain their opinion, and we ask questions rather than criticise personal tastes.

items.prompt: Talk about how cultures influence each other.
items.modelAnswer: Cultures influence each other through food, music, language and travel. For example, international restaurants introduce new ingredients, while local musicians sometimes combine traditional sounds with modern styles.

items.prompt: Make examples with each other and one another.
items.modelAnswer: We help each other when a neighbour is ill, and students teach one another during group work. These examples show how people can share skills and support one another in everyday life.

content.audioTranscript: A: How was the cultural exchange? B: Great. The students stayed with a local host family. A: Did they learn about local traditions? B: Yes, and they practised the language every day. A: Did they attend the town festival? B: They did. The whole community was involved. A: How did the visitors behave? B: They showed respect and made new friendships.
